Caterpillar Inc. v. Lewis.place_name: Near Louisa, Lawrence County, Kentucky (site of the July 9, 1988 bulldozer fire)
Caterpillar Inc. v. Lewis.evidence: Sixth Circuit: "On July 9, 1988, plaintiff James David Lewis, a resident of Louisa, Kentucky, was injured while he was operating a Caterpillar D8K bulldozer... While plaintiff was operating the bulldozer near Louisa, Kentucky, a hydraulic hose... ruptured." (Lewis v. Caterpillar, Inc., No. 94-5253, 6th Cir. Oct. 11, 1995, unpublished)
Caterpillar Inc. v. Lewis.notes: The Supreme Court opinion in the casebook says only 'Kentucky'; the Sixth Circuit's opinion in the same case places the accident near Louisa. Lewis's employer was Gene A. Wilson Enterprises, Inc.; the exact job site is not given in any available source. A Gene A. Wilson with a Louisa office (101 Madison St) appears in other filings, but it is not confirmed to be the same business, so the pin is Louisa's center, from Google Maps.

Exxon Mobil Corp. v. Allapattah Services.place_name: U.S. District Court, Southern District of Florida (Wilkie D. Ferguson Jr. U.S. Courthouse), Miami - where the dealers' class action was filed
Exxon Mobil Corp. v. Allapattah Services.evidence: "In 1991, about 10,000 Exxon dealers filed a class-action suit against the Exxon Corporation in the United States District Court for the Northern District of Florida." (the Court's wording)
Exxon Mobil Corp. v. Allapattah Services.notes: The pin is the court where the dealers' suit was initially filed. The casebook and the Supreme Court opinion's own text say the Northern District of Florida, but the case record shows otherwise: the dealers' action is Allapattah Services, Inc. v. Exxon Corp., No. 91-0986-Civ (S.D. Fla.), 61 F. Supp. 2d 1308 (1999), tried to a jury in Miami before Judge Gold and then appealed to the Eleventh Circuit (333 F.3d 1248). The facts are a nationwide dealer-overcharge scheme with no single site. The companion case, Ortega v. Star-Kist, was filed in the District of Puerto Rico. Address and coordinates from Google Maps.

Minton v. Gunn.place_name: Tarrant County civil district courts (Tom Vandergriff Civil Court Building), Fort Worth, Texas
Minton v. Gunn.evidence: Court of Appeals (Fort Worth): "On August 25, 2004, Minton filed this legal malpractice action against appellees..." The trial court granted summary judgment for Gunn, and "Minton appealed the judgment to the Second Court of Appeals in Fort Worth."
Minton v. Gunn.notes: The pin is the court where the malpractice suit was filed. The opinions do not name the trial court or county; they say the suit was filed in state court on August 25, 2004 and appealed to the Second Court of Appeals in Fort Worth, and both sides' appellate counsel were in Fort Worth. That points to a Tarrant County district court (the Second Court also covers Denton and other nearby counties); the county is inferred and not confirmed from the docket. The pin is Google Maps' marker for the Tom Vandergriff Civil Court Building, where Tarrant County's civil district courts sit. Minton's earlier patent suit was in the Eastern District of Texas, Lufkin Division; no source places the TEXCEN lease to R.M. Stark & Co.
Minton v. Gunn.address: N Calhoun St, Fort Worth, TX 76102

Jacob & Youngs, Inc. v. Kent.place_name: George E. Kent's "Jericho House," Jericho, Long Island, New York
Jacob & Youngs, Inc. v. Kent.evidence: Appellate Division, 187 A.D. 100 (1919): the building contract of May 5, 1913 was for "a private residence for the defendant at Jericho, L. I."; Cardozo: work "ceased in June, 1914, and the defendant then began to occupy the dwelling."
Jacob & Youngs, Inc. v. Kent.notes: Cardozo's opinion says only 'a country residence'; the Appellate Division's opinion places it at Jericho, Long Island (Nassau County), and Old Long Island blog posts identify it as 'Jericho House,' the George Edward Kent estate, built 1913-14 by Jacob & Youngs and later demolished. It stood near Jericho Turnpike (NY 25) close to the Ralph J. Preston estate 'Ivy Hall,' but no source gives an address or coordinates, so the pin is Google Maps' marker for the hamlet of Jericho, not the house.
